The DNS seems to have been the issue most people were facing. It was a failure of the dns network in general. I've run many a site and had configured this the same as all but having connected to multiple dns servers around the world I found inconsistence that means that the dns system itself could not get on the same page. It may relate to having cloudflare'd the site right away. That involves setting your name server to one of theirs. Namecheap started broadcasting the records it had, cloudflare did as well. Going to servers around the world there were some that had the www record but not root. There were some that had root but not the www record. People obviously were able to see videos yet others could not.

It sounds like what the world needs is some sort of proof of consensus engine. Like some sort of blockchain.

Dropping cloudflare seemed to resolve the issue. I'm hoping that if I stay off cloudflare for a while and let the records settle and then swich to cloudflare later I hopefully will have the same experience I've had with every other site I've run which is non-interruption. I don't know if I can claim that cloudflare interrupted my site because I did switch over before it could be considered running.
